_comment:
'Once per Turn Instant - 0: Reveal the top card of your deck. Put a Mechanologist item of the same color from your banished zone on top of your deck.'

The activated ability was SEARCH_BANISH_FACE_DOWN, which is trap_door's effect and runs the card BACKWARDS: it searches your DECK, banishes what it finds FACE-DOWN, and SHUFFLES. So a free activation milled a card out of the deck and shuffled it, where the card retrieves one INTO the deck and must not shuffle -- putting something on top and then shuffling is putting it nowhere. Its 'destination': 'deck_top' was read by nothing.

SEARCH_BANISHED is the banished-zone twin of SEARCH_GRAVEYARD (same may-fail-to-find shape, same destination handling) and did not exist. 'Of the same color' is a comparison against the card just revealed, not a literal colour: REVEAL_TOP_DECK stores it under a ref and SAME_COLOR_AS reads it. The old version hard-coded color 'yellow' in an effect-level gate, which is both the wrong question and the wrong moment.

'Once per Turn' needs no authoring: the card DB parses it from the printed text (has_per_turn_limit=True, activations=1) and play.py enforces it when the activation is OFFERED. A once_per_turn param here would be a second implementation of a rule already handled, which is how two copies of one rule end up disagreeing. Crank is printed. The enters-with-a-counter and the start-of-turn steam upkeep were already correct.

abilities._comment: Was a plain STATIC, so the counters were never placed. 'Enters the arena with N counters' happens ONCE, when it enters -- an ON_ENTER_PLAY trigger, not a continuous static, which would have kept adding counters had it run at all.
